title: Synergistic Management of Abandoned Cropland Mitigates Trade‐Offs Between Food Security and Climate Mitigation in Hilly and Mountainous Areas
content:
Abstract

Abandoned cropland is a crucial strategic reserve to reconcile food security (SDG 2) and climate mitigation (SDG 13). However, maximizing these co-benefits in ecologically fragile hilly regions is constrained by intense spatial competition between food and carbon. In this study, we proposed a spatial decision-making framework that integrates suitability assessment and Pareto optimization to quantify trade-offs and identify synergistic pathways in a typical hilly province of Southwest China. The results showed that although the remaining abandoned cropland had substantial potential for either food (4.0 × 1011 kcal yr−1) or carbon (1.38 × 106 t CO2 yr−1), the dual-suitability overlap rate reached 69.1%, leading to high opportunity costs under single-objective management. Crucially, scenario simulations and Pareto analysis identified Pareto-efficient compromise solutions for balancing regional benefits. When spatial prioritization was combined with intensified management, food and carbon potentials could be increased by 125.0% and 51.6%, respectively, without expanding beyond abandoned cropland. These findings highlight that governing abandoned cropland in complex terrain requires spatially differentiated zoning that distinguishes food-dominant, carbon-dominant, and synergistic management zones to achieve regional synergistic gains.
